Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The pedestrian fatality chart is credited by the manual to a federal highway source; its three speed and risk pairs are stated as printed in the chart text [A04].
The variable speed sign page shows an example sign whose reading is only an illustration; no example number from it is taught as a rule [A03].
The stopping distance chart lists five distances in feet, but the matching speeds are not in the extracted text, so only the football field comparison at sixty mph is stated and the chart values are held as debt [A12] (verify OR-LANE-D-STOPCHART).
Pavement marking meanings come from the captions beside each diagram; the diagrams themselves are not in the extracted text, so part C declares a visual surface for marking recognition.
Interstate limits are stated by the manual only as varying, so no interstate number is taught.
